A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GEM for supervised fine-tuning, despite the changed title and substantial revision. All 28 pages of each version, including v1 Appendices A–E and v2 Appendices A–G, are readable. Shared algorithms, identical loss code and retained appendix examples establish correspondence.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama-3-8B fine-tuning experiments using UltraFeedback, MetaMathQA and Magicoder-OSS-Instruct, with instruction-following, diversity, mathematical reasoning and code-generation results.

after.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning comparisons across models from 3B to 70B parameters, including diversity, downstream performance, forgetting and hyperparameter-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: v2 adds a beta=0 prototype that transfers logits from the highest-probability token and stops when the label becomes maximal (Sections 4–5). The practical positive-beta method retains the same detached auxiliary distribution, log-sigmoid weighting and sequential data reset; Listing 1's executable code is unchanged.

E1.justification: UltraFeedback training and AlpacaEval, GSM8K and HumanEval evaluations remain. v2 removes domain-specific training on MetaMathQA and Magicoder-OSS-Instruct, plus IFEval, poem/story writing, MATH and MBPP evaluations. It adds ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA and WinoGrande evaluations, substantially changing task coverage.

E2.justification: NEFT joins CE and CE+WD in the chat, HumanEval and GSM8K comparisons. CE+Entropy disappears from those quantitative comparisons, although its appendix diagnostic remains. Pre-trained models become explicit diversity and forgetting references. v2's GEM corresponds to the earlier GEM-LS implementation, so that name change is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: The main setup changes from Llama-3-8B to Llama-3.1-8B and adds Qwen-2.5-3B/7B, Gemma-2-9B and Llama-3.1-70B configurations. GSM8K response sampling changes from 32 to 16, and a new diversity comparison uses 100 AlpacaEval questions with a five-shot pre-trained reference. LoRA configurations are introduced, although their assignment is inconsistently documented.

E4.justification: v2 adds beta sensitivity, direct pre-training versus SFT diversity analysis, and parameter-distance analysis of forgetting (Tables 2–3 and Figure 7). Appendix F.5 adds concrete failure details and examples to v1's brief discussion of unsuccessful training without data reset. The quantitative linear-versus-log-sigmoid comparison and three-prompt distribution analysis disappear; the CE+Entropy tail diagnostic remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Both use multiple generated responses for point estimates. v2's discussion of reduced training-gradient variance does not introduce experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced or added. For example, AlpacaEval BoN@32 CE/GEM-LS scores are 46.61/49.46 in v1 Table 4, versus CE/GEM scores of 47.3/50.4 in v2 Table 3. The different stated base models prevent interpreting this as a same-setting improvement. v2 adds forgetting, sensitivity and cross-model results while removing the earlier instruction-following, creative-writing and specialized-training result sets.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal CE logit-flow conservation result and revises v1's stationary-point theorem into a unique Nash-equilibrium statement with an explicit positive-support assumption and expanded proof. The reverse-KL optimizer is retained, while the auxiliary entropy coefficient is corrected from 1/beta to beta. The rewritten log-sigmoid formulation in Appendix B introduces a derivative-sign inconsistency despite unchanged implementation.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes reduced overfitting, lower perplexity, better IFEval performance and gains from specialized fine-tuning. v2 centers its contribution on a probability-transfer game, preserving pre-trained diversity, comparable direct-generation performance, reduced sampling costs and mitigation of forgetting. Broader model scalability and alignment-tax reduction become central claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly argues that diversity-preserving sparse updates protect pre-trained knowledge and interprets smaller parameter displacement as supporting reduced forgetting. It adds substantive discussions of inference-temperature adjustment, architectural explanations for weight decay's limitations and non-uniqueness at beta=0. Appendix F.2 also gives ambiguous guidance about beta's entropy effect relative to the main theoretical relationship.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GEM repository link, NEFT noise scale 5, LoRA rank 16 and expanded computation/memory accounting; the full loss listing and core training recipe already existed. Details for removed experiments disappear. Some new disclosures conflict: Appendix E retains the old base-model name, and Appendix F.4 excludes 70B from LoRA while Figure 10 labels that model as using LoRA.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands around alignment tax, game-theoretic learning and imitation/inverse reinforcement learning. Appendix A.1 adds a detailed comparison with SPIN. Newly cited work includes NEFTune, catastrophic-forgetting studies and maximum-entropy inverse reinforcement learning. The earlier cognitive-science and neuroscience motivations are removed, substantially changing the argument's relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and technical narrative are extensively rewritten. New sections organize the paper around challenges, probability transfer and game theory. Related work moves from Section 2 to Appendix A, and sequential-method development moves into Appendix B. Ethics and reproducibility statements are added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the overview schematic, adds probability-transfer and controller diagrams, and reorganizes empirical displays into sampling curves, scatterplots and model-comparison panels. Many earlier benchmark tables and bar charts disappear. The tail-probability plot and sentence examples are retained as Figure 9 and Table 1. Conference formatting also substantially changes headers, typography and layout.

improvement.justification: Pre-trained controls, beta sensitivity and tests across model families strengthen evidence beyond v1's single-model study. However, quantitative CE+Entropy and specialized-training comparisons are lost, while the central new forgetting magnitude is difficult to reconcile across the introduction, Section 6.2 and Figures 6–7. New loss-sign and LoRA-setting inconsistencies further limit confidence. These substantive benefits and harms leave the net change in overall quality uncertain.
